questions.topic: How much music a ritornello contributes
questions.learningObjective: Estimate a ritornello's contribution

stimulus.body: The city memo shows a ritornello form with a two-bar refrain recurring five times and three two-bar episodes.

questions.stem: While marking a score, How many bars does the ritornello refrain contribute in total?
questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: two bars times five occurrences is ten bars. On that basis "Ten bars, counting five occurrences" is the supported choice. Option A ("Two bars, counting one occurrence") fails because it undercounts recurrences; Option B ("Four bars, counting two occurrences") fails because it undercounts by three; Option D ("Six bars, counting three occurrences") fails because it undercounts by two.
questions.hint: Multiply refrain length by recurrences.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What makes a double fugue double
questions.learningObjective: Explain what makes a double fugue double

stimulus.body: A short reference note on what makes a double fugue double is set for a close-reading task. It states: The two subjects are combined in counterpoint. A marginal reminder adds: think of simultaneous presentation. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: This task depends on “Explain what makes a double fugue double / Think of simultaneous presentation. / What makes a double fugue double”. Which option best satisfies it?

options.text: They are played in different tempos

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the two subjects are combined in counterpoint. On that basis "They are combined in counterpoint" is the supported choice. Option B ("They are unrelated in key") fails because it confuses double fugue with modulation; Option C ("They are played in different tempos") fails because it confuses double fugue with polymeter; Option A ("They are identical") fails because it confuses double with repetition.
questions.hint: Think of simultaneous presentation.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The subject material of a double fugue
questions.learningObjective: Describe the subject material of a double fugue

stimulus.body: The city memo shows a double fugue whose first subject is a rising fourth and whose second subject is a falling third.

questions.stem: While marking a score, How many distinct subjects does that double fugue present?

options.text: Three subjects, adding an extra theme
Zero subjects, using free counterpoint only
options.misconception: reverses the direction of the reasoning the passage sets out

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: a double fugue presents two distinct subjects. On that basis "Two subjects, presented in counterpoint" is the supported choice. Option C ("One subject, repeated twice") fails because it confuses double fugue with restatement; Option B ("Three subjects, adding an extra theme") fails because it overcounts themes; Option D ("Zero subjects, using free counterpoint only") fails because it reverses the direction of the reasoning that settles the subject material of a double fugue.
questions.hint: Count the distinct subject themes.
